note: RFC 7947 Section 2.1: "The route server SHOULD perform one or more BGP Decision Processes to select routes for subsequent advertisement to its clients, taking into account possible configuration to provide multiple Network Layer Reachability Information (NLRI) paths to a particular client as described in Section 2.3.2.2 or multiple Loc-RIBs as described in Section 2.3.2.1." Section 2.3 declares itself informative, so the mechanisms of 2.3.2.1/2.3.2.2 are read as what the decision must take into account, not as normative procedure. Re-judged 2026-10-26 by an independent auditor after ea4394c1fb; supersedes the weak verdict of f725acbf39, whose finding (no carrier for the configuration clause) is closed. Decision clause, client without ADD-PATH: the rfc7947_rs_decision_test.go pair (live bgp-rs/bgp-rib sessions, fenced TCP history) is unchanged in substance: positive, the holder's source re-announcing a worse route leaves the client on B's exact attributes with no withdrawal; negative, a worse later route from B sends the client nothing for P; both discriminated by oweAnnouncement contest -> true. Multiple-paths clause (2.3.2.2): TestRSAnnouncementAddPathClientGetsEveryPath gives client C ADD-PATH send and, in both arrival orders with B worse, asserts on C's wire two NLRI for the prefix with distinct Path Identifiers carrying each source's exact attributes, and zero owed keys; against the decision pair's identical input, this is the configuration-dependent contrast the clause asks for. Its paired record is honest: Ze keeps every path at an ADD-PATH destination through three independent layers (unframed-source identifier allocation in fwdPathIDTable.generate, the fresh-identifier reservation in bindSourcePath when a path meets another owner's slot, and oweAnnouncement's key.addPath guard), each break alone is recorded green because the other two still keep distinct slots, and the three together collapse C to one slot per prefix with the election running there, which is exactly a decision that gives an ADD-PATH client only the elected path (C then receives one path; red at the first-path wait). The test asserts wire outcome, so any other route to that failure also goes red; its arrival-order assertion is stricter than the RFC but not contrary to it. Per-client Loc-RIB clause (2.3.2.1): TestRSOwnerWithdrawalPolicyDeniedSkipsToNextSurvivor gives C an export policy denying B; after the owner A withdraws, C receives E's exact attributes with no withdrawal and never B's route (the per-client best after the client's policy, i.e. no path hiding), and with E denied too, exactly one withdrawal; the mutant recoveryStagedAnnouncement synthesizedWithdrawal branch -> true makes the denied B the replacement and C is withdrawn. Auditor probe, scratch only (HEAD export, not committed): the Section 2.3.1 Figure 1 case at arrival (C holds permitted worse E, then B's better route, denied for C, arrives) keeps C on E with no withdrawal; it stays green with the forwarded-withdrawal foreign-owner guard in adjOutWrite.allow disabled (and all four x-5 tags stay green under that break), and goes red (C withdrawn) only when the carrier's recoveryStagedAnnouncement mutant is added, so arrival-time path hiding rests on the same egress step-past the tagged carrier discriminates, behind the RFC 4271 ownership guard. Residual, not a finding against this row: no x-5 carrier combines an ADD-PATH client with a per-client export policy, and the arrival-time Figure 1 case has no tagged unit of its own.
